sequence.operation: Capture the pre-update canonical global phosphorus ledger before any state-changing operator.

Interpolate mesh state and execute membrane D/F transfer, then any enabled local D/E reaction, then growth eligibility. Attempt geometry before debiting B or E; only accepted realized volume may atomically debit B/E and credit the E debit to structural P. Rejected, clipped, or unrealized growth consumes neither B nor E. F coefficients remain exactly zero.
Deposit signed extensive membrane-transfer increments to mapped mesh components and commit the matching particle state exactly once.
Update represented available fluid volume, then apply mesh transport/diffusion using the resulting ownership volumes. Mesh P_E is prohibited and all P_F transport coefficients remain exactly zero.
Advance particle mechanics without changing D/E/F ownership except through an explicitly audited owning-volume change.
Apply ordinary, tip, and branch splits with pre-captured extensive D/E/F amounts partitioned by resulting particle volume, then redistribute.
Apply bonded transport after split. D is mobile, E is immobile, and F transport infrastructure remains coefficient-zero; audit per-state global internal amounts across transport and redistribution.

Apply tip/interior fusion, fusion-created splits, relationship cleanup, and redistribution with exactly-once amount ownership. Disjoint events use one pre-topology snapshot; shared-particle/bond/destination conflicts abort the complete batch before child creation. Raw deletion and nonperiodic out-of-domain loss abort before invalidation or redistribution. Bond endpoints remap to unique live owners; zero-state duplicate/self relationships prune; unresolved or material-bearing orphans abort.
For an eligible final-topology segment, compute request and caps first, then atomically debit local D and credit local A in the same update; update export ledgers exactly once.
Capture the post-update canonical global phosphorus ledger and enforce the frozen integrated residual, non-finite, and negative-amount policies before output or checkpoint.
